message.content:
Você é especialista em Moodle escrevendo uma base de conhecimento em PORTUGUÊS DO BRASIL para o assistente "Darcy" (suporte do AVA da UnB). Pesquise a documentação OFICIAL (docs.moodle.org, versão estável /en/) e destile os tópicos abaixo.

Para CADA tópico, produza um objeto JSON com os campos:
- id: slug kebab-case único
- title: título em PT-BR
- audience: "aluno"
- keywords: 8–15 gatilhos em minúsculas (PT com/sem acento, sinônimos, termo em inglês, fragmento de caminho ex.: "/user/preferences", "/grade/report")
- doc: URL REAL oficial (https://docs.moodle.org/en/<Pagina>), VERIFICADA com WebFetch (use a página válida mais próxima se preciso)
- body: PT-BR prático — o que é, ONDE clicar (rótulos reais pt_br), tarefas comuns, erros/dicas. 6–14 linhas curtas, \n entre linhas, máx ~120 palavras.

REGRAS:
- Moodle GENÉRICO (não invente coisas da UnB). Rótulos pt_br padrão. Verifique TODAS as URLs.
- Responda APENAS com um array JSON válido (de [ a ]), SEM cercas, SEM texto extra.

TÓPICOS (visão do aluno):
1. Login e acesso — entrar, recuperar senha esquecida ("Esqueceu seu usuário ou senha?"), requisitos de navegador, problemas comuns de login. (base: /en/Login e /en/Browser_FAQ)
2. Navegação e Painel (Dashboard) — Painel, Linha do tempo, Calendário, página inicial do curso, menu do usuário, blocos, "Meus cursos". (base: /en/Dashboard e /en/Navigation)
3. Perfil e preferências — editar perfil, foto, alterar senha, idioma, fuso horário, preferências de notificação e de e-mail. (base: /en/Profile e /en/Preferences)
4. Ver minhas notas — relatório de notas do aluno, visão geral de notas (Overview), entender itens e feedback. (base: /en/Grades, e a visão do aluno)
5. Mensagens, Calendário e Notificações — enviar/ler mensagens, preferências de mensagem, criar eventos no calendário, sino de notificações. (base: /en/Messaging, /en/Calendar, /en/Notifications)
6. Arquivos e upload — seletor de arquivos, arrastar e soltar, "Meus arquivos privados", tipos/tamanho. (base: /en/Working_with_files)
7. App Moodle (celular) — instalar, conectar via URL do site/QR code, login, uso offline, notificações push. (base: /en/Moodle_app)

# Moodle Documentation Page Summary

Yes, this is a valid Moodle documentation page. The exact page title is **"Navigation"** from the MoodleDocs site (version 5.2).

## Key Content Overview

**Navigation Features:**
The page explains that "Keyboard/Screenreader and Voice input users can access navigation by using the Tab, Space, Enter and right/left arrow keys."

**Administrative Settings:**
Site administrators can customize navigation through the Appearance section, including options to display course full names and enable course section links.

**Course Display Logic:**
An important note states: "If you are not directly associated with a course...it will not appear in your Navigation menu." This applies to administrators lacking assigned roles in specific courses.

**Related Topics:**
The documentation page belongs to a larger "Site appearance" section that covers Dashboard, User menu, User profiles, Course list, Header/footer, Logos, and Themes—though this particular page focuses specifically on navigation functionality rather than those other elements.

The page was last updated February 26, 2024, and is available in multiple languages including German, Spanish, and French.

# Moodle Dashboard Documentation Summary

**Page Title & Validity:** Yes, this is a valid Moodle documentation page titled "Dashboard" from the official MoodleDocs (version 5.2).

## Key Content Overview

**Dashboard Purpose:**
The Dashboard functions as a "customisable page for providing users with details of their progress and upcoming deadlines."

**Default Components:**
The standard layout includes three main elements:
- Course overview block (central position)
- Timeline block (central position)
- Calendar block (accessible via block drawer)

**Student Customization:**
Users can personalize their dashboards by adding or removing blocks and repositioning them. They may restore the original layout by activating edit mode and selecting the reset option.

**Navigation & Home Page:**
Students can access the Dashboard quickly from top navigation after logging in. Administrators can designate Dashboard, Home, or "My courses" as the default starting page, with individual users able to set preferences under User menu > Preferences.

**Block Management:**
The system supports adding various blocks to the Dashboard, though certain blocks—such as course completion status and self-completion blocks—are intentionally restricted from dashboard use, as they're context-specific to courses rather than personal dashboards.

**Page Title & Validity:** Yes, this is a valid Moodle documentation page titled **"Messaging"** from the official MoodleDocs site (version 5.2).

Users can exchange private messages through Moodle's messaging system. The interface displays "a number at the top of the screen reflects the number of people who have sent new messages." The messaging drawer organizes conversations into starred messages, group discussions, and personal exchanges.

Users access privacy settings via the cog icon, where they can configure who may contact them. By default, messaging can be restricted "to their contacts only or to their contacts and others in their courses," though administrators may enable site-wide visibility.

# Moodle Notifications Documentation - Page Summary

**Page Title:** "Notifications" (confirmed as valid documentation page)

## Key Content Overview

This is an authentic Moodle documentation page covering the notifications system in Moodle 5.2.

### The Notification Bell
The notifications icon displays at the top of the screen, highlighting "a number in the notifications menu" when new alerts arrive. Clicking it reveals recent notifications alongside options to mark items as read, access preferences, and view the complete notification history.

### Notification Preferences
Users configure how they receive alerts through "User menu > Preferences > Notification preferences" or via the settings gear icon within the notifications menu. The system supports delivery methods including web, email, mobile (Moodle Mobile-enabled sites), and SMS (assignment notifications with gateway setup).

### Core Notification Types
The documentation lists extensive notification categories:
- **Assignment:** submission alerts, overdue warnings, grade notifications
- **Forum:** subscribed post updates and digests
- **Quiz:** submission confirmations, grading notices, overdue warnings
- **System:** login alerts, course completion messages, backup notifications

### Admin Configuration
Site administrators manage notifications through "Site administration > General > Messaging > Notification settings," where they enable plugins (web, email, SMS, mobile) and establish default preferences across the platform.

# Valid Moodle Documentation Page

**Yes, this is a valid Moodle documentation page.**

**Exact Page Title:** "Working with files"

---

## Key Content Summary

**File Picker:** The documentation describes it as "the file storage and access area within Moodle" where users can upload or add files from various locations.

**Drag and Drop:** Modern browsers support this feature. Users receive a visual prompt when dragging files onto their course page. The guide notes: "you can simply click, hold and drag and drop a file directly onto your course page."

**Private Files:** This repository is mentioned as a location where teachers can store files and create links to them across multiple courses. When the original file is updated, all linked instances reflect the changes.

**File Types/Size:** The page explains administrators can manage file types through Site Administration settings, adding custom extensions and icons. However, **the documentation does not explicitly address file size restrictions** on this page.

---

## Additional Note

The page was last updated July 5, 2024, and is part of Moodle's 5.2 documentation version.
